Additionally, I can mechanically verify: head -c against the known 1120 bytes from the previous probe (size=1120 in ls). Now, compare the first 1120 bytes against… there's no byte image of the previous file. But the recorded size 1120 is from the ls before this turn's append; the current file must have a prefix ≥ 1120. Verify the current size, and confirm that the first 1120 bytes end exactly at the previous newline? This isn't a hash-based proof but a size consistency check. Honest receipt: the snapshot was lost between turns (tmp cleanup), so the prefix proof for this turn = (a) >> semantics, (b) the cat read-back of the previous line matches word-for-word with the previous turn's read-back, (c) the size transition of 118→1120→the new size. State it that way; do not overclaim.
